scores.visual_critic_note: Restrained monochromatic palette and clever color-as-mark encoding in the scatter panel show real design intent, but the force network is too dense to read (labels collide badly in the core) and the color scatter dots are too small at rendered size to compare distributions across hue ranges.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Honest encoding throughout: bar chart Y-domain starts at 0, both circle-size scales use scaleSqrt, all domains are data-driven via d3.extent/d3.max, no dual axes, no quantile traps, and no line chart requiring defined() handling.
scores.stress_test_note: RAF dirty-flag pattern properly coalesces rendering, but the O(n) bitFilter.set() computation runs on every brush mousemove rather than being deferred to the flush, creating sustained CPU pressure at 60fps during drag.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Four crossfiltered views (timeline brush, 60-node monochromatic network, HCL color scatter, block list) stay within working memory limits and form a coherent spatial hierarchy, but the color scatter is dense enough that individual dot clusters are hard to parse at a glance without hovering.
flags: Partial Update Storm: bitFilter.set() iterates ~34K blocks synchronously on every brush mousemove event (unthrottled data computation), though DOM updates are correctly RAF-coalesced via the dirty-flag pattern

proposer: 956 lines, down from 960. Moved JS axis styling and brush selection styling to CSS, inlined `thresholds` variable. Net -4 lines. The color view axis text will now use 10px (matching timeline) instead of 9px — a negligible visual difference that improves consistency.
